name: redmine
label: Redmine
description: Issue tracker: find issues, read them, comment, change status and assignee.

list_issues.doc: find issues; params go into the query as Redmine expects them (project_id, status_id, assigned_to_id, sort, limit)

get_issue.doc: read one issue including its journals; params: id

comment.doc: add a note; params: id, issue={"notes":"…"} (Redmine nests everything under issue)

update_issue.doc: change status, assignee or priority; params: id, issue={"status_id":N,"assigned_to_id":N,"priority_id":N}

prompt_doc:
Redmine is your issue tracker. The base URL and the API key come from the platform — you never see them.

Redmine nests request bodies under a single key ("issue"), so pass that object as one parameter rather than flat fields. Read an issue before you comment on it: the journals hold the history you are answering to.
